fields.System.Title: RPL-2 — Reactive replenishment
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Notice when a pick face has dropped below its minimum, find stock to refill it with, and create
exactly one task.

Scope

In. Below-minimum detection, source selection, task creation, duplicate prevention,
no-source alerting.

Out. Predicting demand before it happens — that is [RPL-4](RPL-4-demand-driven.md).

Design notes

RPL-204 decides whether this epic is useful or a nuisance. The trigger fires on every
stock movement. During a wave, a popular pick face receives twenty movements in two minutes,
each one below the minimum. Without a check for an existing open task, that is twenty tasks for
one shortage.

Enforce it with a unique constraint on (location_id, status) where status is open, so the
database rejects the second insert under concurrency. A check-then-insert in application code
loses the race.

Source selection order: same product, available status, FEFO batch order, prefer a source
that covers the whole need in one trip, then prefer nearest.

RPL-205 must reach a human. A no-source condition logged and forgotten means the pick
face runs dry mid-wave and pickers short-pick. It belongs on the supervisor's exception list,
not in a log file.

Decide the precedence rule against allocation explicitly. Both want the same bulk stock. A
reasonable default: replenishment for a released wave outranks allocation for an unreleased
order. Whatever you choose, write it down — otherwise it is a race.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Task storm | [doc 09 §7.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| No source found and nobody told | [doc 09 §7.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Competing with allocation for bulk stock | [doc 09 §7.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Task created for a blocked location | [doc 05 WF 11](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
